routeSelection.route: Dutch-language track, with the Dutch Language and Usage package
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the generic Dutch Language and Culture bachelor. The current OER offers a Dutch-language subject-specific track and a partly English Crossing Borders track; the subject-specific track most directly represents the programme's Dutch-language-and-culture identity. Its two equally formal depth packages respectively emphasize language/use and Dutch-language literatures. Neither is clearly more general, so the first-listed package, Nederlands: taal en gebruik, is selected by official order. Methods and Statistics 1 is likewise the first-listed compulsory method option. These choices were fixed independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Three plans are supported through general literary and linguistic methods, communication and cultural study. The broad plan balances these strands, the language option emphasizes cognition, rhetoric and digital text analysis, and the literature option emphasizes interpretation, adaptation and cultural institutions. The introductory Dutch course supports practical language use. Historical Dutch, Dutch philology, advanced Dutch linguistics and the Dutch-language thesis are material gaps. Crossing Borders remains an official direction and the chosen three plans fill the available slots.

alternatives.label: Language, Literature and Culture
alternatives.labelReason: Study how people use language and interpret stories. Combine literary analysis, rhetoric, media and history with psycholinguistics and introductory Dutch. Use qualitative, historical and digital methods to explore texts and culture.
alternatives.concept: Study how people use language and interpret stories. Combine literary analysis, rhetoric, media and history with psycholinguistics and introductory Dutch. Use qualitative, historical and digital methods to explore texts and culture.
progression: Brain and behavior precedes psycholinguistics. Literary and media introductions precede adaptation and independent interpretation.

alternatives.label: Language, Communication and Digital Society
alternatives.labelReason: Study language acquisition, style and persuasion alongside public communication and digital media. Learn how to analyze text data and examine language models and their ethical implications. Introductory Dutch provides practice in everyday language.
alternatives.concept: Study language acquisition, style and persuasion alongside public communication and digital media. Learn how to analyze text data and examine language models and their ethical implications. Introductory Dutch provides practice in everyday language.
alternatives.distinctness: Study language acquisition, style and persuasion alongside public communication and digital media. Learn how to analyze text data and examine language models and their ethical implications. Introductory Dutch provides practice in everyday language. Each plan has 6 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1.
progression: Brain and behavior precedes psycholinguistics. Programming, introductory data analysis and mathematics precede neural networks. Introductory rhetoric precedes public rhetoric practice.

alternatives.label: Literature, Media and Cultural History
alternatives.labelReason: Read literature across genres and traditions and study how stories move between text, film and other media. Explore cultural history, identities and institutions through literary criticism, visual culture and creative work.
alternatives.concept: Read literature across genres and traditions and study how stories move between text, film and other media. Explore cultural history, identities and institutions through literary criticism, visual culture and creative work.
alternatives.distinctness: Read literature across genres and traditions and study how stories move between text, film and other media. Explore cultural history, identities and institutions through literary criticism, visual culture and creative work. Each plan has 7 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1. Each plan has 11 courses absent from the other when compared with option 2.
progression: Literary and media foundations precede advanced interpretation and adaptation. Art history precedes museum and art-historical study.

blocks: Both develop close reading and literary interpretation across forms and genres.
Utrecht studies modern Dutch-language texts. UCR studies works from a range of literary traditions.
Utrecht studies early modern Dutch-language texts and culture in a dedicated course.
Utrecht studies medieval Dutch-language texts and cultures in a dedicated course.
Both study language and cognition. UCR’s Psycholinguistics focuses on acquisition and processing across languages.
Both analyze how choices in style, wording and structure shape meaning.
Utrecht examines meaning and language development specifically in Dutch. UCR studies related processes across languages.
Both study how language shapes communication. UCR approaches this through rhetoric and argument.
Both study audience, persuasion and effective communication.
Both connect reading and writing. UCR develops creative work across forms and media.
Utrecht examines Dutch grammar, structure and variation. UCR’s Dutch course develops practical introductory language skills.
Utrecht teaches corpus methods for Dutch studies and uses them to prepare students for the thesis. UCR develops general text-data skills.
Utrecht offers a dedicated comparison of Dutch languages and varieties.
Utrecht studies Dutch identity specifically. UCR examines identity and representation in a broader cultural context.
Utrecht studies multilingualism and literacy in a dedicated course.
Both develop research design and statistical analysis.
Utrecht requires a 7.5 EC thesis in Dutch after the corpus course. UCR offers optional 15 EC independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Choose 52.5 EC of electives, including a coherent 30 EC profiling package.

notes.text: The UCR options offer related study in language, literature, communication and culture, including introductory Dutch. Utrecht’s degree focuses throughout on Dutch languages, literatures and cultures.

Utrecht includes dedicated medieval and early modern Dutch texts, Dutch linguistic variation, corpus methods and a thesis in Dutch. The UCR plans develop related analytical and research skills across languages and cultures.

audience.programmeDescription: This Utrecht bachelor studies Dutch languages, literatures and cultures across periods, media and social settings.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example follows the fully Dutch-taught track and emphasizes Dutch language and usage. The UCR plans explore related questions through language and cognition, communication, literature and cultural history.
